# Effect reference

This file is generated from `src/effects/types.ts` and `src/effects/bleed.ts`. Regenerate it with `node scripts/gen-effect-reference.ts` after any change to the effect table; do not edit it by hand. Every default and every bleed figure below is computed by the same code the renderer and the checks use.

The narrative — when an effect carries information and when reaching for one is a mistake — is at [EFFECTS.md](EFFECTS.md).

## Reading the bleed column

**Bleed** is how far past an element's own bounding box the effect puts ink, in SVG user units. It is what the `effect-within-canvas` check measures against the canvas, and what the repair loop grows `canvas.padding` to accommodate. An effect that bleeds nothing can never be clipped.

The figures below are for each effect **at its default parameters**. Bleed scales with the parameters — a larger `blur` or `radius` reaches further — and composes through a chain in order, so a `blur` placed after a `shadow` spreads the shadow's already-offset edge as well.

## Effect kinds

The ten primitives. Any of these may be written inline in a spec as an object with a `kind`; the named effects in the next section are compositions of them.

| kind | parameters and defaults | bleed at defaults | follows a block's label | drawn as |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `shadow` | `dx` = `0`, `dy` = `2`, `blur` = `6`, `color` = `"#000000"`, `opacity` = `0.4` | left 9, top 7, right 9, bottom 11 | no — surface only | SVG filter |
| `glow` | `radius` = `8`, `color` = `"#5B8DEF"`, `intensity` = `0.85` | 12 on every side | no — surface only | SVG filter |
| `blur` | `radius` = `3` | 4.5 on every side | yes | SVG filter |
| `occlusion` | `radius` = `5`, `dx` = `0`, `dy` = `2`, `color` = `"#000000"`, `opacity` = `0.55` | none — stays inside its own bounds | no — surface only | SVG filter |
| `brightness` | `amount` = `1.15` | none — stays inside its own bounds | yes | SVG filter |
| `saturate` | `amount` = `1.2` | none — stays inside its own bounds | yes | SVG filter |
| `tint` | `color` (required), `amount` = `0.3` | none — stays inside its own bounds | yes | SVG filter |
| `grain` | `amount` = `0.15`, `scale` = `0.8`, `seed` = `7` | none — stays inside its own bounds | yes | SVG filter |
| `bevel` | `depth` = `2`, `azimuth` = `235`, `elevation` = `45`, `strength` = `0.6` | none — stays inside its own bounds | no — surface only | SVG filter |
| `sheen` | `strength` = `0.12`, `direction` = `"down"` | none — stays inside its own bounds | no — surface only | painted geometry |

**follows a block's label** distinguishes an effect describing the block as an object (a shadow belongs to the surface; a label with its own shadow is embossed lettering) from one describing its whole appearance (a blur that left the label sharp would read as a bug). See EFFECTS.md for why a block is two SVG elements in the first place.

| `inset` | `occlusion` → `brightness` | none — stays inside its own bounds |
| `lit` | `sheen` → `occlusion` → `shadow` | left 15, top 11, right 15, bottom 19 |
| `printed` | `grain` | none — stays inside its own bounds |

| `raised-3` | `shadow` | left 30, top 22, right 30, bottom 38 |
| `recede` | `blur` → `saturate` → `brightness` | 3 on every side |

## Canvas vignette

`canvas.vignette` takes a number from 0 to 1 and darkens the figure's edges. It is not in the table above because it is not a node effect: it is painted over the finished figure as a radial wash, bounded by the canvas by construction, so it has no bleed and can never be clipped. A value outside 0–1 is a `SpecError`.
